data.body: [P2] Do not clear terminal-delivery history at every invocation boundary. If callbacks A and B are created before either is awaited, invocation 2 can consume A and suspend on B without checkpointing. After B completes, invocation 3's first checkpoint returns A again because its sequence remains above `handler_seen_seq`; this cleared set lets `on_operation_end` fire twice for A, producing duplicate terminal spans or an unresolved-parent error when nested. Retain delivery accounting per execution until terminal completion, or persist per-operation acknowledgement of successful invocation-input delivery, and add a regression covering this two-callback sequence.
